notes.title: Burnouts & Buffs. This Update Hits Harder.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/4deb64b0191b0302ca55531b5218e3d8341d0573.png[/img]

Hi gang!

It's been a month and 10 days since the last demo update and we're back for another!

While a lot of our time and effort has been on content beyond the demo region, we've still managed to have a significant number of changes for the demo. 

I'll leave you with a list of highlights followed by the detailed release notes, that might be interesting to someone.

[b]Suggestions and feedback are very welcome![/b] Come talk to us on [url=https://discord.gg/d56vheUkR4]Discord[/url] or here on the Steam forums!

[h2]Highlights[/h2]
[h3]Major Rework of Aiming:[/h3]
We've heard from quite a few of y'all in the feedback forms about the un-good aiming in the previous version. The aim assist was aggressive and sticky, it was required for aiming to work at all, the mouse movements would get stuck on the corners, and aiming behind the car was clunky and unintuitive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/5ceec8479b5806fc2a4379f1905f66e22d543ce2.gif[/img]

We've been trying a lot of things out and we're happy enough with the progress so far to add it in this update. There were many little changes and fixes that I won't go into, but the gist is that the aim should just feel better now, as we've fixed all the issues I mentioned in the first paragraph and then some. Importantly Aim assist is no longer required to be playable, it acts more like a magnet to targetable things and is only enforce on flying units; since aiming controls are horizontal only, this is still needed. I still think some aim assist is more fun with this kind of control scheme, but it's optional now. Additionally, the reticle now interacts directly where you're aiming at, instead of finding hotspots to lock onto, helping to feel more responsive.

Also in this update, we've added many more [b]aiming poses for Lucky[/b] so she can track targets vertically and instead of blocking Lucky at the back angles, she'll snap into the other direction immediately so it feels seamless to aim backwards (she contorts herself a bit, but we're prioritizing function over form today).

[h3]Burning Rubber Upgrade feelin' oomphy:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/d79b3958484371a9b83c94852ed6565308386a81.gif[/img]
It just feels nice to use now. When you have this upgrade, use the "Heavy Drift" button to use it. Left Ctrl on keyboards, Left Trigger on gamepads.

[h3]Balance Changes:[/h3]
I'm using a lot of big sounding adjectives in this update, but I mean it, lotsa things. All player weapons have had some changes with a focus on "feel and function" first and balance in close second. Effective DPS is fairly similar between weapons, but it depends on the target. Each gun has it's favoured usecase:
[list]
  [*] Shotguns focuses on being effective against large, or many targets, at a close range. It's easy to aim, but not all pellets will hit the target.
  [*] Burst rifle focuses on being effective against one or two target sweeps at medium range. It's fairly easy to aim, but the bullets travel slower than the Power Rifle and can miss.
  [*] Power Rifle focues on being effective against single targets at far range. It hits hard, has a higher chance to "crit", upgradable crit damage, and has the unique chance of piercing through a target to hit others. It reloads slowly, as a downside.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/1dc28bef40508f92afc57969f8ae5bc1229960ec.gif[/img]

Many permanent and temporary upgrades have also had a balance pass. Eg. Scoville's fire effects are more effective now, while Berzerk and Double Shot have been nerfed a bit.

[h3]Status Effect Descriptions:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/e8b9e1f69b318916368c1a312781c0797d182991.png[/img]
Before this version, there was no way to know what the "Inspire", "Intimidated", "Burning", "Berserk", etc... status effects were actually doing. These are now described along with the Reaper upgrade that unlocks them.

[i]Note: "-30% seconds" in that upgrade description is not on purpose, it should read -0.03 seconds I think. That's on me, I messed up.[/i]

[h3]Gamepad ForceFeedback[/h3]
The ForceFeedback is important to sell the feeling of firing a weapon or smashing into a car. I've gone over much of the effects we had in there and adjusted it for my Xbox Series controller, especially for things that happen often. I've reduced a lot of the frequent extremes that felt a bit annoying on the hands, and made some of the guns feel more crunchy.

[h2]Detailed Release Notes for v0.7a-7[/h2]
I like reading release notes, figure someone else out there might too.

[b]Forest Boss[/b]
[list]
  [*] Fixed Musical Note Bombs triggering damage more than once and causing WAY too much damage
  [*] Improved the Boss' movement to better keep his distance from the player
  [*] Added a specialized boss camera for a better and smarter view of the combat arena
  [*] Slightly increased the boss health and balanced his attack damage/speed
  [*] Fixed the boss death animation to properly play the mass blood-feast animation
  [*] Improved the Boss' attack visual tells, vfx, and sfx
  [*] Added a pre-beat visual and audible tell for the Lead Guitar speaker beam attacks
  [*] Added a new Vincent Von Velvet health bar, with his proper name displayed and faction colours
  [*] Fixed popping and missing Foliage LOD meshes during the boss fight
  [*] Trees now go translucent to get out of the camera's way
  [*] Fixed some attacks ignoring the player armor when they shouldn't have
  [*] Updated Vince's Blood Feast vfx to better line up with the victim
  [*] Fixed boss combat music never ending after dying
[/list]
[b]Devil[/b]
[list]
  [*] Added a specialized camera view when the devil appears
  [*] Devil Screenshake now persists and instead lowers its intensity dynamically
  [*] Fixed the rapid disappearance when the devil leaves the scene
  [*] Added new sound effects and demon presence ambiance
  [*] Fixed a bug where the Devil's darkness effects and sounds would not disappear
[/list]
[b]Graphics[/b]
[list]
  [*] Reduced Autodetect benchmark requirements to attain Medium settings (as we optimize the game, the graphics requirements for higher settings can lower)
[/list]
[b]Upgrades and Status Effects[/b]
[list]
  [*] Increased damage and better explained effects for:  Burning status effect caused by Burning Rubber, Brick Oven, and Screaming Hot Shot (Scoville upgrades)
  [*] Significantly improved the look, sound, and feel of "Burning Rubber"
  [*] Burning and Decay status effects now ignore armor (damaging health directly)
  [*] Camera will now zoom out to show effects of Burning Rubber
  [*] Reaper Upgrades will now describe their status effects on hover
  [*] Overall improvements to Reaper Upgrade descriptions, especially those that replace weapons
  [*] Changed BoneLance spikes to always be extended and to have all forward lances at level 1
  [*] Changed the visual effect on "Shielded" and Decay
[/list]
[b]Misc Combat[/b]
[list]
  [*] Swapped gamepad button for LockOn target to Right Shoulder (left trigger is already in use for drifting)
  [*] Fixed cases where armor could take damage on the wrong side when hit
  [*] Fixed a bug where Hellhounds could start an attack after being killed
  [*] Added more Combat Quip dialogues
  [*] Added cap to damage resistance (max 95% damage resisted)
  [*] Reworked many of the Gamepad force feedback effects
[/list]
[b]Balance[/b]
[list]
  [*] Rebalanced the drop rate of cash and junkparts
  [*] Slightly increased bullet speed (6000cm/s to 8000cm/s)
  [*] Many changes to the player weapons and weapon upgrades were made in this build. Focusing on "feel" and DPS balance.
  [*] Took a pass at Permanent Upgrade prices (Demo only supports up to max level 3 for all upgrades)
  [*] Many of the Enemy stats and behaviors were adjusted in this update (damage, health, speed, aggressiveness)
[/list][b]Enemies[/b]
[list]
  [*] Cultist behavior will now focus aggressively on the chained-down target
  [*] Increased cultist animations and reaction time
  [*] Increased aggressiveness and improve positioning for the ATVs
[/list]
[b]Bugs[/b]
[list]
  [*] Improved suspension physics to be more stable at low framerates
  [*] Improved vehicle movement when facing the opposite direction, reduced situations where enemy vehicles would rapidly accelerate in the wrong direction
  [*] Fixed a crash during chain throws from cultists
  [*] Fixed Vehicle Engine sounds playing when paused
  [*] Fixed Cultist chains from flipping and flopping about
  [*] Fixed Burst Rifle and Power Rifle to use the proper force feedback settings
  [*] Fixed the broken chains on the vampire Cultists
[/list]
[b]Aiming[/b]
[list]
  [*] Added vertical aiming for Lucky
  [*] Improved aiming responsiveness, especially when wrapping around to the other side
  [*] Fixed mis-aligned 2H weapon poses for Lucky that were offset from the actual aim direction
  [*] Fixed the 2H gun hovering above the left hand
  [*] Changed the Aim reticle to follow the tip of the aim beam instead of being based on aim assistance. This was a bit of an overhaul so feedback is definitely appreciated here.
[/list]
[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
  [*] Fixed Vampire Bat Swarms tanking framerates and improved their targetability, movements, and animations
  [*] Fixed several VFX that would stay around, slowing the game more over time
  [*] Plus lots of minor things not worth itemizing
  [*] Fixed Burst Rifle and Power Rifle to use the proper force feedback settings
[/list]
[b]UI[/b]
[list]
  [*] Added animations to the Weapon HUD UI
  [*] Fixed the "click to continue" mouse icon in dialogues to properly change with the input mode
[/list]

notes.title: Steam Deck and Handheld Support
notes.content:
[h3]Playable on Steam Deck?[/h3]

[b]YES![/b] Fully playable with good performance in our internal testing (with Proton).

[h3]Performance Snapshot[/h3]

As of the July 16th demo build, v0.6a-35, we're able to run the game, at low/medium mixed settings, consistently well above +30fps on the Steam Deck OLED and ROG Ally (with Windows) while unplugged, usually above 40fps. The game currently uses just a bit above 20w with these settings, though it does spike while loading threads are active.

We intend to keep the game running smooth on these handheld devices in all future updates and to improve power usage where we can.

[h3]Recommended Graphical Settings[/h3]
[list]
  [*] Medium for most settings
  [*] EXCEPT Global Illumination and Reflection Quality (set these to Low)
  [*] Resolution: Deck @ 1280x800, ROG Ally @ 1280x720p
[/list]
Higher resolutions are playable, but expect increased battery usage (up to ~30W on Ally).

[i]Note: The game does run ok on medium settings, though there are some hitches and slowdowns, so reducing a few Graphical settings to low can help with that, eg. Global Illumination and Reflection Quality.[/i]

[h3]Need Help, Have Suggestions, or Want to Chat?[/h3]
Come talk to us on Discord!
https://discord.gg/d56vheUkR4

Thanks for playing!
Al - Lead Programmer

notes.title: New Demo!
notes.content:
[p]Hey there reapers!
[/p][p]Here's the latest gossip: Scaravan 66 will NOT be in early access this July. While we announced, not too long ago, that it would be heading to Early Access, we've decided to delay this and instead refresh the demo while the full game bakes a little longer.
[/p][p]Development is going very well, the other areas are being fleshed out, and our enemy roster is really filling up! BUT with all of the feedback we've received, we want to spend a little more time tweaking and polishing while we can, before putting it out there.[/p][p]
The good stuff: New Demo!,[/p][p]
As I've mentioned, we've got a new demo up on Steam.[/p][p]
The release notes for all the changes can be found [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3238240/view/528726587469725765"]here[/url] [/p][p]
Here's what's up, we've put a lot of work into the game game since we released the early preview demo during February's Steam Next Fest, and while we can't do EA just yet, we could keep updating the demo and treat it like a type of early access with a smaller scope, and as a bonus: demos are FREE! So that's what we intend to do![/p]

notes.title: DevLog 10: Meet The Cast: R.I.P. Tide Posse
notes.content:
Hailing from the sunny and deadly, R.I.P. Tide Coast, this gang of beach bully bad boys also happen to be half-shark half-men, 100% Sharkmen. When they aren’t partying on the beach with bodacious babes, or hanging ten on some gnarly waves, they are wreaking havoc on the highways along the coast. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/b981f58d713d9b9e0646f6b6212d8c152f0ed986.png[/img]

Very little frightens them, more confident in a puka necklace and socks with sandals than anything else, there are only two things they fear, the devil herself and the meanest of them all: their ruthless and mysterious leader, Johnny Splash. [NOT pictured. Headshots are $20, autographs are $50]

Equipped with jet skis and the raw unmatched power of their incredible shark teeth, this shiver of sharky bad boys are on the hunt to stop Lucky from reaching the end she would be so close to achieving in their territory.

notes.title: DevLog 9: Meet The Cast: Theta Theta Psi Sorority
notes.content:
Almost unintelligible with insider lingo speak, these late teens, early twenties kids of rich families got where they are by selling their souls to the devil and making multi-generational demonic pacts. For many, participating in evil rituals about sacrificing innocents are some of their earliest and fondest memories with their parents. 

Their parents attend secret society meetings where they plan to buy and corrupt politicians, blackmail world leaders, and use the media to manipulate the masses. These Socialite kids, meanwhile, mostly just attend parties, get messed up, or go joyriding in their expensive cars and commit the occasional murder for the fun of it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/506f0975941dcf45c90f7c717101d219b4958b7f.png[/img]

They are so similar. Are they all related? No, they just go to the same plastic surgeon, and the same personal trainer, and wear the same matching outfits, and think the same thoughts, and anyone even one inch shorter or taller than the rest get subbed in for ritual sacrifice during rush week. Many dark rituals are performed by their wealthy parents during their adolescence to make sure their daughter is exactly an acceptable Theta Theta Psi five feet and six inches by the time she is a pledge. Don’t begin to ask what evils they’ve done to ensure that they have no cellulite.

The demonic magic that got them their fashionable possessions saturates them, enabling them to be used for random acts of violence. Normally content to attack other drivers and pedestrians, these sorority girls have had their demonic contracts activated and now turn their evil designer brand items to dealing with Lucky.

notes.title: DevLog 8: Meet the Cast: Ximena
notes.content:
No-nonsense and cheeky flirt mechanic Ximena loves to help. She’s no pushover, but she loves to flex by showing off her strength and skills. Need your oil changed? Easy work. Want help moving a couch? No problem, she’ll do most of the lifting. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/71ff03465f89364f77275e6dbd7826291df54b26.png[/img]

While she’s almost comically determined to prove herself, she plays it really cool. She prefers to joke and keep things light, and despite all of her friendly efforts, she keeps people at an arm’s length and separate from her inner world. Before her death on Route 66, she had worked as a local mechanic and lived nearby even longer, though her home often changed. She’s one of the few reapers who didn’t die passing through.

notes.title: DevLog 7: Meet the Cast: The Zomboyz
notes.content:
The Zomboyz are a chaotic band of zombified psychobilly punks. Addicted to adrenaline, carnage, and rock’n’roll, they have a joint mission of both stopping Lucky and seeing how far they can send their limbs flying in a radical explosion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/9eac511b431ed7c95c57754a42e21e6e3ce437eb.png[/img]

The Zomboyz originate from an epic concert in the desert, set up by a famous Psychobilly band. Trying their best to make a memorable rager, the band turned to ancient demonic texts and rituals for inspiration for the show. Unknowingly, the texts and symbols possessed real magic and they accidentally turned the entire wrecking pit into unwitting sacrifices to the devil. Instantly dead, and instantly rebirthed as the undead, many of the crowd, caught up in how metal it all was, willingly threw themselves into the sacrificial circle to be “wrecked” as they later would call it. The hard-core circumstances of their creation made them eternal servants to the devil and to the creation of ungodly and bombastic (with emphasis on the bomb) chaos. 

To this day, the most hardcore adrenaline seekers return to the site of that concert to be wrecked and join the legions of carnage loving zombie freaks.

notes.title: DevLog 6: Meet the Cast: The Skeleton Crew
notes.content:
In the 1950’s, the military experimented with nuclear weapons in the desert. In one tragic incident, experimenting with a new novel form of radiation, something went horribly wrong. Many died. The bases were closed down, and the entire situation was covered up. That was not the last of those sickly souls, however, and through the unknown properties of the strange radiation, their irradiated corpses rose once again. Their flesh melted off, revealing walking skeletons, glowing from the radiation that they themselves now emit. 

Now these former soldiers and military scientists continue their former goals of advancing their scientific and technological knowledge to create powerful weapons. Working out of their long-abandoned bases and working with whatever old tech they can scrounge up and repair, they develop and employ deceptively high-tech weapons and vehicles which they use to defend their territory. They are no longer bound by the rules of a government, nor to mortal morality. They have become The Skeleton Crew. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/d7e530bfba6787f08d6fef83234b16b2f452a2ae.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/231e2d40f87ced80b73dea200a4e04e61257a76a.png[/img]

notes.title: DevLog 5: Meet the Cast: The Fratwolves
notes.content:
Hey hey, Andy here again. 

Happy Friday! 

Today we are going to learn about the first gang you encounter in Scaravan 66: The Fratwolves.

Loud, aggressive, athletic, and dumber than a bag of jock-straps. The Fratwolves are a gang of college football players who intentionally became infected with lycanthropy to get that extra edge on the field. The original werewolf bite was provided in a deal with the devil, which came with the hefty cost of eternal servitude, but can you really put a price on the best football season of your college career? Everything would be going perfectly, or rather it would be, if they could just get practice in or stop missing their games. Unfortunately, one little annoying Road Reaper keeps driving off of her section of Route 66 and into the territory the Fratwolves are tasked with policing. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/6357b8fec2e3a8ad14321d2fe63cfa13c9e70a6f.png[/img]

No time to party, no time to practice, no time for brewskis with the broskis. Being the closest gang territory to the Junkyard where the local reapers hang, and not so coincidentally where Lucky D keeps starting her carnage, the Fratwolves are most frequently called upon and therefore bothered by Lucky D. Tired, frustrated, but still pumped with team-spirit and that lycan rage running through their veins, the Fratwolves remain steadfast on stopping Lucky dead in her tracks.

That's all for today!

-andy out

notes.title: DevLog 4: Meet the Cast: Molly Morgue
notes.content:
Hey there! Andy again. Coming at you a day late because frankly I forgot what day of the week it was. 

Today we are learning a little about Molly Morgue! 


Mysterious and vibrant, Molly doesn’t have any regrets from life. Death-obsessed and with a dark sense of humour, Molly has never felt more at home than in the after-life. Once a doghouse bass player with dreams of being in a Psychobilly band, in life she aspired to raise the roof  and steal the show with her wicked bass playing, however Molly discovered that in death her instrument had the ability to raise and command the dead instead. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/774a3739fd62dd857aa58058e92013a184d4fdb4.png[/img]

Frankly, as she found out, that's all she ever wanted in the first place. A captive audience who does as she bids. As a new necromancer and a lifetime control freak she enjoys the power she wields, which is not insignificant given the job that was thrust on her as a Road Reaper. Maybe the only reaper who isn’t confused or upset about how they wound up here, Molly knows not to look a gift-horse in the mouth and enjoys her new unlife as much as she can. 


That's all for today! Check back on Friday to find out if I remember what day of the week it is or up from down. 

-andy out

notes.title: DevLog 3: Meet the Cast: Mimosa Ron
notes.content:
Hey hello! It's Andy again!

Happy Friday! Today we're going to meet another one of the cast members of Scaravan 66: Mimosa Ron!


Former mathematics professor, Ron had only just started his retirement and was ready to live it up when he met a terrible fate along Route 66, awaking to find that he was now doomed to reap souls. Ron had only just left the workforce and found himself back in the drudgery of working life.

Determined to reclaim his retirement years and the cruise he was supposed to take, Ron does the least he possible can in order to fly under the radar of the ever watchful demons who keep the reapers in line. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/6b4c968420dd8618386007e5928cf9b4a62901dc.png[/img]


While a lot of reapers are rough, tough and prefer hard liquor,  Ron spends most of his time sampling the most delicious umbrella decorated tiki cocktails and having a good time. If he’s not blending a frozen margarita he’s sunning himself in the sand or putting his feet up in a hammock. In death he has discovered he has quite the knack for cocktail mixing, so much that he is able to imbue special magic into drinks that he makes. All the fun, none of the bad side-effects, but with a little magical kick to the drinker’s skills and abilities.

Always a good time, but hard to get to know the real him. He lives behind a wall of outward joy, laughter, and irresponsibility. Ron is a champion of not taking things seriously and not letting the world get in his head or in his way of having a great day.


That's all for today! Check back on Tuesday for another DevLog and be sure to try the demo and wishlist Scaravan 66 now! 


-andy out

notes.title: DevLog 2: Meet the Cast: Scoville
notes.content:
Hey hello! It's Andy again! 

Today we're going to take some time to meet one of the cast members of Scaravan 66: Scoville! 

Scoville is a Road Reaper and a powerful ally of our hero Lucky D. He gives fire-related upgrades at pit stops that'll make even the fiercest minions of hell sweat. 

Once a hitchhiker, traveling cook, and odd-jobber, Scoville could charm anyone with a word or a pot of chili. Wearing his heart on his sleeve didn’t always pay off in life, but it never made him jaded, only wiser. If bad experiences were hard lessons and hard lessons made a wiser man, then Scoville knew it all. He wasn’t one to raise his voice, but not one to roll over either. If you are lucky enough to call him friend or neighbour, you can’t pass by without being offered some of his latest experimental culinary creations or comforting favourites. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/8c42b63c41e005a3efd9f6772eb2f213a3c033f6.png[/img]

After coming to an untimely road related incident on Route 66, Scoville awoke as a Road Reaper. Forced to reap souls for what all he knew was eternity. Frustrated as anyone would be, he soon discovered he was not the only one and took great pride in giving his community of road reapers a needed touch of warmth and hospitality. He discovered that in death he had the power to imbue his food with magical properties, a by-product of walking the line between the world of the living and dead. With his new found power he could cook up a meal to the specific needs of his friends. A little cheer-up soup here, a little courage brisket there. A skill so useful (and delicious) he really solidified his position as a leader in the community. 

Scoville is one of the most loved and appreciated by his fellow reapers on Route 66. Everyone always makes time for Scoville, because he always makes time for them.


That's all for now! Check back on Friday for the next DevLog and be sure to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3238240/Scaravan_66/]try the demo and wishlist Scaravan 66[/url] today!


-andy out

notes.title: Demo Update 0.5.1
notes.content:
Hey folks!

Firstly, thank you so much to everyone who has been sending in feedback! This has been so helpful in understanding what can be improved and what it feels like to be newly introduced to the game (first impressions!)

[h2]Update Overview[/h2]

We've just pushed an update that fixes a game breaking bug on the death screen, some effects to help clarify how some systems work, and some UI work.

I hope you're all having a lovely weekend!

[h2]Release Notes 0.5.1[/h2]

[b]Critical Issues:[/b]
- Fixed a bug causing the game to get stuck on the Death screen

[b]Gameplay feel:[/b]
- Added a hit-pause on ram (sometimes not always)
- Added a few more explosion camera shakes
- Engine Overheat: Reduced the delay before engine cooling starts up from 2 seconds to 1
- UI and Engine/Bumpers now Flashes when overheating
- Engine now steams until it has cooled

notes.title: DevLog 1: Saying "Hi" and Shouting "LIVE Demo"!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/ea3202edd6f162d35711b890d0b0e776ea93e51d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45288720/8fcf5202d93741866fa1cbb69a2b31805518d659.png[/img][/url]
My name is Andy, and along with my partner Al, we’re going to excitedly introduce you all to the world of Scaravan 66 in this series of devlogs. Starting with this one — Today! Right now!

So as you’ve probably already read in the description on the store page, Scaravan 66 is a high-octane car combat roguelike. In silly baby terms? This is a game about boom boom zoom zoom, go faster, get stronger, shooty shooty. That and with a light dusting of existential dread and absurdist philosophical themes.

As of the publishing of this dev-log, you can [b]download the free demo[/b] on Steam, in a pre-alpha state! The game is still [b]under-construction[/b] and there are features that are not yet available. For example, the demo is VERY light on narrative (sorry, no major spoilers in this one!), has very little voiceovers, and focuses on early gameplay loop and combat. 

We are very open to feedback as we want to make sure we craft this to be a great experience for everyone. No matter how much we test ourselves, it’s invaluable to hear feedback from real players. So, we greatly appreciate any comments or responses you provide through our survey.

Al and I plan to release a dev log [b]every Tuesday and Friday[/b] so make sure to check back on those days to learn more about the game, the narrative, and the eclectic cast of characters in Scaravan 66!

Download that Demo and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3238240/Scaravan_66/]Wishlist on Steam[/url]!
